name: How do you add storage in a walk-in shower without making it look crowded?

mainEntity.name: What is the best way to include shelves, niches, or benches in a walk-in shower without cluttering the design?
mainEntity.text: What is the best way to include shelves, niches, or benches in a walk-in shower without cluttering the design?

acceptedAnswer.text: The cleanest way to add storage is to plan it into the shower from the beginning instead of treating it as an afterthought. Recessed niches are usually the most space-efficient option because they keep bottles off the floor and do not project into the shower area. A single bench can be useful for seating or shaving, but it should be sized so it does not crowd the shower floor. In larger showers, one or two well-placed niches often look better than multiple shelves because the design stays streamlined. The exact placement should consider shower head location, tile layout, and how the shower will be used every day. Storage should also be waterproofed correctly so the feature does not become a leak point. A well-designed shower feels calm and open, with storage integrated into the walls rather than bolted on afterward.
acceptedAnswer.description: Built-in niches and a single bench usually provide the cleanest storage in a walk-in shower. The best results come from planning storage into the wall layout before tile installation so it looks intentional, not added later. Too many shelves can make the shower feel busy and harder to clean.
